Namespace: Wolfgang.Extensions.String Assembly: Wolfgang.Extensions.String.dll Syntax public enum AcronymHandling Fields Name Description AsWord The acronym is cased like any other word: SKUCode becomes SkuCode. This is what the conversions do when no options are given. Preserve A word that has no lower-case letter is left as it is wherever a word is capitalized: SKUCode stays SKUCode in Pascal case. api/Wolfgang.Extensions.String.WordBound.summary: Enum WordBoundaries The things that divide one word from the next when a case conversion splits a string. Namespace: Wolfgang.Extensions.String Assembly: Wolfgang.Extensions.String.dll Syntax [Flags] public enum WordBoundaries Remarks Separators, Delimiters and ControlCharacters only make a difference together with Keep: when punctuation is dropped, every character that is not a letter or a digit ends the word whatever is chosen here. Fields Name Description All All of the above. This is what the conversions use when no options are given. CaseChanges A change of case inside an identifier: an upper-case letter after a lower-case letter or a digit, and the last upper-case letter of a run that a lower-case letter follows. ControlCharacters A character for which IsControl(char) is true, such as a tab or a line feed. Delimiters An underscore or a dash, the delimiters of snake case and kebab case. None Nothing divides words except what Drop removes. Separators A character for which IsSeparator(char) is true: a space, a no-break space, a line or paragraph separator.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Wolfgang.Extensions.String
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Install dotnet add package Wolfgang.Extensions.String Or from the Package Manager Console: Install-Package Wolfgang.Extensions.String In Visual Studio, search for Wolfgang.Extensions.String in Manage NuGet Packages. Use Add the namespace, then call the methods on any string: using Wolfgang.Extensions.String; // Substring helpers (null-tolerant, length-clamped) "A sample string".Left(8); // "A sample" "Hello".Left(10); // "Hello" "Hello".Left(0); // "" "A sample string".Right(6); // "string" // Center padding "Hello".PadCenter(11); // " Hello " "Hello".PadCenter(11, '-'); // "---Hello---" "Hello".PadCenter(3); // "Hello" (already wide enough) // Case conversions "A sample string for processing".ToCamelCase(); // "aSampleStringForProcessing" "A sample string for processing".ToKebabCase(); // "a-sample-string-for-processing" "A sample string for processing".ToPascalCase(); // "ASampleStringForProcessing" "A sample string for processing".ToSnakeCase(); // "a_sample_string_for_processing" "a sample string for processing".ToTitleCase(); // "A Sample String For Processing" // Case conversions with your own word rules var keep = new CaseConversionOptions { Punctuation = PunctuationHandling.Keep }; "Hello, World!".ToSnakeCase(keep); // "hello,_world!" var acronyms = new CaseConversionOptions { Acronyms = AcronymHandling.Preserve }; "SKUCode".ToPascalCase(acronyms); // "SKUCode" // The words themselves "SKUCode for user_login!".SplitWords(); // "SKU", "Code", "for", "user", "login" Supported frameworks Target Version .NET Framework 4.6.2 and later .NET Standard 2.0 .NET 8.0, 10.0 On .NET 8 and later the package has no dependencies. On .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 it depends on System.Memory. Where to next The API Reference documents every overload, its exceptions and an example. The examples project is a runnable console app.

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Wolfgang.Extensions.String
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Wolfgang.Extensions.String is a small library of extension methods for string: Substring helpers: Left and Right return the first or last N characters. They clamp the length (a string shorter than N is returned unchanged) and return null for a null input. Center padding: PadCenter centers a string within a total width, padding both sides with spaces or a character you choose. When the padding is uneven, the extra character goes on the right. Case conversions: ToCamelCase, ToKebabCase, ToPascalCase, ToSnakeCase and ToTitleCase. The package is published on NuGet as Wolfgang.Extensions.String and targets .NET Framework 4.6.2, .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 8.0 and .NET 10.0. Behaviour worth knowing ToCamelCase, ToKebabCase, ToPascalCase and ToSnakeCase split the string into words by one shared rule and differ only in casing and in what goes between the words. A word is a run of letters and digits; every other character (white space, punctuation, symbols, control characters, _ and -) ends the word and is left out, except an apostrophe, which is removed without ending the word. A word also starts at a case boundary inside an identifier, so "SKUCode".ToSnakeCase() is sku_code, "Line2Qty" is line2_qty and "user_login_count".ToPascalCase() is UserLoginCount. They use invariant casing, so the result does not depend on the current culture. Each of the four has an overload that takes a CaseConversionOptions: keep punctuation in the words (Punctuation), choose what divides words (Boundaries), leave acronyms in upper case (Acronyms), or supply your own word splitter (WordSplitter). A new CaseConversionOptions holds the default rules. SplitWords returns the words themselves. ToTitleCase delegates to TextInfo.ToTitleCase of the current culture, and leaves words that are entirely upper case unchanged. PadCenter and the case conversions throw ArgumentNullException for a null input. Left, Right and PadCenter throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a negative length or width. Next steps Getting Started: install the package and call each method. Building from source: build, test and contribute. API Reference: every member, generated from the XML doc comments.

docs/setup.html.summary: Building from source Prerequisites .NET 10.0 SDK. The test project also targets older frameworks; tests for a framework run only when its runtime (or, for .NET Framework, Windows) is available. Optional: PowerShell 7 for the scripts under scripts/.
